q: 1. The height of capillary rise is maximum in
explain: Capillary rise is inversely proportional to pore/particle size; colloidal (extremely fine) soils have the smallest pores and hence the greatest capillary rise (though very slow).

q: 2. The quantity of seepage of water through soils is proportional to
options: total head loss through the soil
explain: By Darcy's law, q = k·i·A, and since i = head loss/length, seepage quantity is proportional to both permeability and total head loss.

q: 3. The neutral stress in a soil mass is
options: stress taken up by the pore water
stress taken up by solid particles
explain: Neutral (pore-water) stress is the portion of total stress carried by water in the pores, as distinguished from effective stress carried by the soil skeleton.

q: 4. The coefficient grain size of soil (D10) is 0.3 mm, the value of coefficient of permeability as per Hazen is (coefficient of Hazen C = 10) .............
explain: By Hazen's formula, k = C x D10^2 = 10 x (0.3)^2 = 0.9 mm/sec.

q: 5. When a cohesionless soil attains quick condition, it looses
explain: In quicksand condition, effective stress becomes zero due to upward seepage force equalling submerged weight, so the soil loses both its shear strength and bearing capacity.

q: 6. The shearing strength of a cohesion less soil depends upon
explain: For cohesionless (frictional) soils, shear strength s = σ tanφ depends primarily on the normal/confining pressure acting on the failure plane.

q: 7. When compared to deformation of thin soil sample because of consolidation, the deformation of thick soil sample will be .............
explain: Because the thick sample has a longer drainage path, its rate of consolidation is slower, so within a given time it shows less deformation than a thin sample (though its eventual total settlement is larger).

q: 8. The expression for the discharge (Q) through a flow net for isotropic soils is given by
explain: For an isotropic soil, seepage discharge Q = K·H·(Nf/Nd), where Nf is number of flow channels and Nd is number of potential drops.

q: 9. The earth pressure in the retaining wall is
options: proportional to internal friction of the soil
explain: Lateral earth pressure at any depth p = K·γ·z increases linearly with depth z, so the pressure (intensity) itself is proportional to depth.

q: 10. On attaining quick condition, cohesionless soil loses its
explain: In quicksand condition, effective stress vanishes, so the soil loses both its bearing capacity and its shear strength simultaneously.

q: 11. The net bearing pressure which can be used for the design of foundations .............
explain: Net allowable bearing pressure is the design value used for proportioning foundations, accounting for both shear failure and settlement limits.

q: 12. The value of net allowable bearing pressure is .............
options: minimum of net safe bearing capacity and net safe settlement pressure
explain: The net allowable bearing pressure is taken as the smaller (more conservative) of the net safe bearing capacity and net safe settlement pressure.

q: 13. Primary consolidation of soil is due to the expulsion of .............
explain: Primary consolidation results mainly from the gradual expulsion of free (absorbed) pore water from the soil under load.

q: 14. The total discharge from two wells situated near to each other is .............
options: sum of the discharges from individual wells
greater than the sum of the discharges from the wells
less than the sum of the discharges from the wells
explain: Interference between the drawdown cones of nearby wells reduces the effective hydraulic gradient, so combined discharge is less than the simple sum of individual well discharges.

q: 15. Total lateral earth pressure is proportional to
options: angle of internal friction of soil
explain: Total pressure (force) on a wall = ½·K·γ·H² (area under the triangular pressure diagram), making total earth pressure proportional to the square of the retained depth H.

q: 16. In order to increase the FS against piping .............
options: a blanket of impermeable material is laid for same length along the downstream ground surface
pump out the water periodically, downstream
explain: Placing an impervious blanket downstream lengthens the seepage path and increases the weight resisting uplift, raising the factor of safety against piping.

q: 17. The seepage flow through a porous medium is generally .............
explain: Seepage velocities in soils are typically low enough (low Reynolds number) that flow is laminar, satisfying Darcy's law.

q: 18. Criterion for the design of an inverted filter is .............
options: D15 of filter/D85 of base < 5 < D15 of filter/D15 of base
D15 of base/D15 of filter < 5 < D15 of base/D15 of base
D15 of filter/D15 of base < 5 < D85 of filter/D85 of base
D15 of base/D85 of base < 5 < D85 of base/D85 of base
explain: The inverted filter design criterion ensures the filter is permeable enough (via D15/D85 ratio) yet fine enough to retain base soil particles.

q: 19. The bearing capacity of soil
options: depends on the size of the footing
explain: Bearing capacity theories (e.g., Terzaghi's) show the ultimate bearing capacity depends on footing size/width (through the Nγ term), among other footing and soil parameters.

q: 20. Direct measurement of permeability of the soil specimen can be made at any stage of loading in .............
explain: In a fixed ring consolidometer, the sample geometry relative to the ring is known at all times, allowing direct permeability measurement at any load stage.

q: 21. Effective stress is
options: the stress at the particles contact
governing factor for the engineering properties
explain: Effective stress (Terzaghi's principle) is transmitted through particle-to-particle contacts, governs shear strength and compressibility, and is a real, measurable physical parameter — hence all statements are valid.

q: 22. Shear strength of soil is determined by the equation
explain: Coulomb's shear strength equation is s = c + σ·tanφ, where s is shear strength, c is cohesion, σ is normal stress, and φ is the friction angle.

q: 23. The coefficient of electro-osmotic permeability .............
options: is the same as the coefficient of hydraulic permeability
varies in the value over a wide range depending on the size of voids in the soil
varies in value over a wide range depending on the grain size of the sample
is almost independent of the grain size of the soil sample
explain: Unlike hydraulic permeability, electro-osmotic permeability depends mainly on the soil's zeta potential and double-layer properties, staying roughly independent of grain size.

q: 24. Neutral stress refers to .............
explain: Neutral stress is another term for pore water pressure, the stress carried by water in the soil voids.

q: 25. The difference between total pressure and pore water pressure is known as .............
explain: Effective stress = total stress - pore water pressure, per Terzaghi's principle of effective stress.

q: 26. A shallow foundation is defined as a foundation which
options: Has a depth of embedment less than its width
Is resting on the ground surface
explain: By Terzaghi's definition, a foundation is 'shallow' when its depth of embedment (Df) is less than or approximately equal to its width (B), typically Df ≤ B.

q: 27. Stress distribution on the failure plane in the case of a triaxial test is .............
explain: In a properly conducted triaxial test, stresses are applied uniformly across the specimen's cross-section and failure plane.

q: 28. In unconfined compression test, around stress is .............
explain: The unconfined compression test applies no lateral (confining/cell) pressure, so the minor principal stress is zero.

q: 29. Soils with a value for coefficient of permeability ranging between 10^-4 to 10^-6 are classified as .............
explain: This intermediate permeability range (10^-4 to 10^-6 cm/s) defines semi-pervious soils, such as silts.

q: 30. If the shearing stress is zero on two planes, then the angle between the two planes is
explain: Zero shear stress occurs only on the principal planes, and the two principal planes (major and minor) are always oriented at 90° to each other.

q: 31. Consolidation is a process involving
explain: Consolidation is a slow, time-dependent process in which excess pore water pressure dissipates and water is gradually squeezed out of a saturated soil under sustained load.

q: 32. An isobar is
options: Point below ground surface where net pressure is zero
A curve or contour connecting all points below ground surface of equal vertical stress
A curve or contour connecting all points below ground surface of equal horizontal stress
A location where vertical stress is equal to horizontal stress
explain: An isobar (pressure bulb contour) in soil mechanics connects points of equal vertical stress increase caused by a surface load, used to visualize the pressure bulb beneath a footing.

q: 33. Capillary water is held in the interstices of soil due to capillarity forces. The capillary force depends upon .............
explain: Capillary force depends jointly on surface tension, water pressure, and the size of soil pores (which sets the meniscus curvature).

q: 34. Quick sand is
options: A condition in which cohesion is decreased quickly
A sand which can be compacted quickly
A condition in which a cohesionless soil loses its strength because of upward flow of water
explain: Quicksand is not a soil type but a hydraulic condition: upward seepage pressure equals or exceeds the submerged unit weight of a cohesionless soil, reducing effective stress and shear strength to near zero.

q: 35. The stress that is responsible for the mobilization of shearing strength of a soil .............
explain: Shear strength is governed by effective stress (per Terzaghi's principle), not total or pore water pressure alone.

q: 36. For a soil layer with double drainage and thickness H, the drainage path is equal to .............
explain: With drainage possible from both top and bottom, water travels only half the layer thickness, so drainage path = H/2.

q: 37. When analogy is drawn between Darcy's law for flow of water and Ohm's law for flow of current, what is analogous to the quantity of seepage?
explain: In the electrical analogy, seepage discharge corresponds to electrical current, head to voltage, and permeability to conductivity.

q: 38. Consolidation is a process involving .............
explain: Consolidation is fundamentally the slow, time-dependent process of gradual pore water expulsion under sustained load.

q: 39. Total pressure on the vertical face of a retaining wall of height h exerted by the retained earth weighting w per unit volume is
explain: Total active earth pressure force = area of the triangular pressure distribution = ½·Ka·w·h², where Ka = (1-sinφ)/(1+sinφ), giving (wh²/2)×Ka.

q: 40. Secondary consolidation is .............
explain: Per the reference key this is marked 'caused by hydrostatic pressure'; secondary consolidation is more commonly attributed to creep (plastic readjustment) of soil structure.

q: 41. The presence of organic matter in a soil will .............
explain: Per the reference key organic matter is marked as having no effect on permeability in this context.

q: 42. The velocity of percolation is defined as .............
options: the discharge per unit of gross c/s area
the discharge per unit of net c/s area
the discharge per unit of total c/s area
explain: Percolation (seepage) velocity uses only the net (void) cross-sectional area available for actual water flow, not the gross soil area.

q: 43. Select the correct statement. The permeability is .............
options: directly proportional to unit weight, inversely proportional to viscosity
directly proportional to viscosity, inversely proportional to unit weight
directly proportional to both unit weight and viscosity
inversely proportional to both unit weight and viscosity
explain: Per the reference key this is marked as inversely proportional to both; the standard formula (k = C.d^2.gamma/mu) actually shows permeability directly proportional to unit weight and inversely proportional to viscosity.

q: 44. In a consolidated drained test on a normally consolidated clayey soil, the volume of the soil during the shearing will .............
explain: Normally consolidated clay contracts (decreases in volume) during drained shearing, unlike dilative over-consolidated clay.

q: 45. The pressure exerted by water on the soil through which it percolates, is known as .............
explain: The drag force exerted by percolating (seeping) water on soil grains is termed seepage pressure.

q: 46. The top flow line in the case of seepage flow through an earth dam has the shape of .............
explain: The phreatic (top flow) line through a homogeneous earth dam closely approximates a parabola (Casagrande's method).

q: 47. Secondary consolidation of soil is due to the expulsion of .............
explain: Secondary consolidation involves slow expulsion of tightly bound (adsorbed) water and plastic readjustment of soil structure, distinct from primary consolidation's free water expulsion.

q: 48. The time factor for a particular degree of consolidation .............
options: depends upon the coefficient of consolidation
depends upon the distribution of initial excess hydrostatic pressure
explain: For a given degree of consolidation, the time factor Tv depends on the shape of the initial excess pore pressure distribution across the layer.

q: 49. The compressibility of a field deposit is .............
options: the same as that shown by a laboratory sample
greater than that shown by a laboratory sample
smaller than that shown by a laboratory sample
explain: Field deposits often contain natural discontinuities/fissures and larger-scale heterogeneity, making them generally more compressible than small intact lab samples.

q: 50. The ratio of settlement at any time t, to the final settlement is called as .............
explain: Degree of consolidation (Uz) is defined as the ratio of settlement achieved at time t to the eventual final (total) settlement.

q: 51. Falling head permeameter is preferable when soil sample is .............
explain: Falling head permeameters are suited for low-permeability (clayey) soils, where flow rates are too slow for the constant head method to measure accurately.
